title: add-rag-deterministic-replay-simulator-and-tool-echo-sandbox
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: teams building RAG-based agents need deterministic, debuggable replays for flaky tool interactions and nondeterministic model outputs. This PR adds a minimal deterministic replay simulator and a lightweight 'tool-echo' sandbox adapter to make authoring, testing, and telemetry-driven regressions easier. The goal is to provide a reproducible local playground that:
1) records a session with seeded randomness and stable timestamps,
2) replays the same session deterministically across runs,
3) includes a tool adapter that echoes calls and can inject controlled noise for robustness testing, and
4) wires up compact docs and a CI smoke test that validates replay determinism across Python/TS example runners.
What changed:
- examples/rag-replay/: new sandbox runner, recorder, and replay harness (Python + TS stubs).
- examples/tool-echo/: tiny tool adapter (HTTP shim + in-process adapter) that deterministically echoes inputs and can inject per-call seed-based jitter.
- docs/rag/replay.md: developer doc explaining the recording format, seed semantics, and how to integrate with existing RAG authoring flow.
- ci/smoke-replay.yml: new workflow that runs a seeded recording and two replays to validate byte-for-byte determinism (allowing for pinned model hashes or mocked model outputs).
- tests/replay/: unit tests for serializer, seed scheduling, and conflict-free timestamping.
Backwards compatibility: the recorder writes a compact JSONL format and a small manifest; nothing changes existing examples unless users opt into the replay harness.
Migration: README snippets show how to add recorder middleware to an existing agent.
Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: users may rely on model nondeterminism; the replay harness supports "model-mock" and pinned-model-mode to avoid divergence.
- Risk: timing-sensitive code may still diverge on different platforms; the harness normalizes timestamps and uses logical clocks.
Additional context: related to ENG-2145 (replay-driven regression tooling) and SUP-448 (customer report of intermittent tool timeouts).

notes_on_changes: This is deliberately lightweight: the recorder uses a compact JSONL event stream containing logical_clock, seed, event_type, and payload. The replay runner consumes the stream and replays events using the same seeds to any registered tool adapters. The tool-echo adapter is intentionally deterministic and suitable as a drop-in dev-time replacement for networked tools during authoring. The design emphasizes reproducibility over simulating production nondeterminism.
release_notes: Add local deterministic RAG replay simulator and tool-echo sandbox for authoring and CI smoke tests. Useful for reproducing flaky tool interactions and evaluating agent regressions. No breaking changes.
manual_test_instructions:
1) cd examples/rag-replay && python recorder.py --scenario=example_dialog --out=run1.jsonl --seed=1234
2) python replay_runner.py --in=run1.jsonl --mode=pinned-model-mode
3) Repeat step 2 twice; checksums printed by the runner should match. See docs/rag/replay.md for TS runner and feature-flagging the http shim.
